sources.label: Originkit
sources.notes: Free library of ~50 previewable animated components for Framer/React, with copy-ready code behind a free API key. URL confirmed by the user; no explicit licence text was read, so this stays reference-only — take morphology, not code.

sources.label: Magic UI (Border Beam)
sources.notes: Border Beam is one component in Magic UI, an MIT-licensed copy-paste animation library (github.com/magicuidesign/magicui). The user pointed at https://magicui.design/docs/components/globe, so the source is the library rather than a standalone border package. MIT permits reuse, but this pack still stores affordance and state binding rather than copied component code.

sources.label: MotionSites
sources.notes: PAID freemium product selling hero-section prompts for Lovable/Bolt/Cursor/Claude. Prompt text is the product being sold — never copy prompts, prompt fragments, or preview media into this repository. Only the interaction morphology may be abstracted.

sources.label: Dot Matrix
sources.notes: Self-described 55+ free and open-source dot-array loaders (spiral, wave, orbit, sweep, pulse families) with a playground. URL confirmed by the user; the specific licence was not read, so use the abstract loading vocabulary rather than copied SVG or CSS.

sources.label: VibeHub
sources.notes: Visual glossary for vibe coding: frontend, backend, tech stack, AI, Git, and design terms shown through interfaces and real use cases. Confirmed by the user. Supplies naming vocabulary only — terms describe intent and state, they do not replace component contracts.

patterns.label: Purposeful result reveal
guardrails: Use only when new content becomes available.
Do not animate layout-critical geometry or delay access to content.
Preserve the product's information hierarchy and copy.

patterns.label: State-bound attention border
guardrails: Never apply the animated border to every card by default.
Use semantic accent tokens only; no hard-coded effect colors.
Focus visibility must remain stronger and independent from decoration.

patterns.label: Dot-array async progress
guardrails: Keep a persistent text status and expose it through role=status or aria-live.
Do not use animation as the sole progress signal.
Use a static dot arrangement when reduced motion is requested.

patterns.label: Named interaction vocabulary
guardrails: Use terms to describe intent, state, and token binding to an AI.
Do not replace domain concepts or component contracts with marketing language.
Record the chosen term alongside the implementation evidence.

patterns.label: Showcase composition reference
guardrails: Apply to landing or showcase surfaces, not dense operational workspaces by default.
Reference morphology may not override product IA, palette, typography, or copy.
Use locally authored primitives instead of copying third-party code or assets.

rules.label: Reduced motion fallback
rules.statement: Every non-essential motion pattern must define a static, opacity-only, or skipped reduced-motion behavior.

rules.label: Text status accompanies async motion
rules.statement: Loading and working animations cannot be the only indicator; a persistent accessible text status is required.

rules.label: Reference does not override product truth
rules.statement: External visual references may inform morphology and affordance, but product brief, semantic tokens, component contracts, accessibility, and implementation rules remain authoritative.

rules.label: Verify source before implementation reuse
rules.statement: A preview or description is not permission to copy code, assets, prompts, or proprietary source structure; canonical URL and license must be verified first.

rules.label: Dashboard motion stays low-noise
rules.statement: Operational dashboards use motion to explain state changes, not as persistent decorative atmosphere.
